fields.title: What is Whole Life Journey
fields.content:
## What is Whole Life Journey

Whole Life Journey (WLJ) is a comprehensive personal wellness and journaling application that combines AI-driven coaching with structured life management across multiple domains. It serves as a unified platform where users can track, reflect on, and improve every aspect of their lives.

### Conceptual Overview

At its core, WLJ operates on the principle that personal growth is interconnected. Rather than isolated tracking apps for health, journaling, finances, and spiritual growth, WLJ integrates all these domains under a single intelligence layer. This means insights from one area of life can inform guidance in another.

The application supports several major life domains:

| Domain | Module | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| Health & Wellness | `apps/health/` | Weight, vitals, fitness, nutrition, sleep, labs |
| Medical Records | `apps/medical/` | Document scanning, medication tracking, provider management |
| Journaling | `apps/journal/` | Daily reflection, mood tracking, gratitude |
| Faith & Spirituality | `apps/faith/` | Bible reading plans, prayer tracking, devotionals |
| Life Management | `apps/life/` | Goals, tasks, habits, projects |
| Purpose & Growth | `apps/purpose/` | Core values, life purpose discovery |
| Financial Wellness | `apps/finance/` | Budget tracking, financial health |
| Brain Training | `apps/brain_training/` | Cognitive exercises and mental fitness |

### Operational Perspective

As an administrator, WLJ provides:

- **Intelligence Command Center (ICC)** — Monitor and manage all AI engine states, guidance, and predictions
- **Intelligence Observability Dashboard (IOCD)** — Track system health metrics, engine performance, and quality scores
- **Admin Console** — User management, task management, system configuration
- **Automated Intelligence** — 14 AI engines working continuously to generate insights, predictions, and guidance

### Technical Architecture

WLJ is built on Django 5.x and uses a three-phase intelligence pipeline:

1. **Interpretation** (Phase 1) — SUE, SLCME, HTIE parse user intent
2. **Execution** (Phase 2) — UAIO orchestrates domain actions
3. **Post-Execution** (Phase 3) — SAE, PIE, PRIE, PGE, and others generate intelligence

The entire system is deployed on Railway with PostgreSQL, uses OpenAI for AI features, and includes a native iOS wrapper for App Store distribution.

> **Key Principle:** Every user action flows through the intelligence pipeline. Data logged in any module triggers insight generation, prediction updates, and proactive guidance across all domains.

fields.title: Technology Stack
fields.content:
## Technology Stack

Whole Life Journey is built on a modern Python/Django stack optimized for reliability, security, and AI integration.

### Core Framework

| Component | Technology | Version |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Backend | Django | 5.x |
| Language | Python | 3.12 |
| Database | PostgreSQL (prod) / SQLite (dev) | 16+ |
| WSGI Server | Gunicorn | Latest |
| Hosting | Railway | — |
| Build System | Nixpacks | — |

### Authentication & Security

- **django-allauth** — Email-based authentication (no username)
- **django-otp** — Multi-factor authentication (TOTP)
- **Custom User model** — `apps/users/models.py` with `UserPreferences`
- **Bearer token auth** — For mobile API endpoints
- **CSRF protection** — Standard Django middleware
- **CSP nonce** — Content Security Policy for inline styles/scripts

### AI & Intelligence

- **OpenAI API** — GPT models for coaching, analysis, and content generation
- **14 Intelligence Engines** — Custom Python services in `apps/core/ai_*/`
- **Linear Regression** — PRIE predictions using scipy/numpy
- **Markdown rendering** — Python `markdown` library with extensions

### Frontend

- **Server-rendered HTML** — Django templates with Jinja2-style syntax
- **CSS Custom Properties** — Design system variables (`--color-*`, `--space-*`, `--radius-*`)
- **Vanilla JavaScript** — No frontend framework dependency
- **Responsive design** — Mobile-first with breakpoints at 480px, 768px

### Mobile

- **iOS Native Wrapper** — Swift/SwiftUI with WKWebView
- **HealthKit Integration** — 23 health data types synced
- **Keychain Storage** — Secure token management
- **Push Notifications** — APNs for intelligence delivery

### Operational Perspective

The deployment pipeline is fully automated:

```
git push → Railway detects → Nixpacks builds → Procfile runs:
  1. fix_stale_migrations
  2. migrate --noinput
  3. load_initial_data
  4. collectstatic
  5. gunicorn serves
```

All fixtures and data migrations run automatically on every deploy via `load_initial_data`, which uses `DataLoadConfig` to track what has already been loaded.

### Key Dependencies

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `openai` | AI coaching and intelligence |
| `markdown` | Rendering Markdown content |
| `pdfplumber` | Medical document scanning |
| `scipy` / `numpy` | Statistical predictions |
| `Pillow` | Image processing |
| `django-allauth` | Authentication |
| `django-otp` | MFA support |
| `gunicorn` | Production WSGI server |

fields.content:
## Application Structure

WLJ follows standard Django project conventions with 20+ apps organized by domain.

### Project Layout

```
dbawholelifejourney/
├── config/              # Django settings, URLs, WSGI
├── apps/
│   ├── core/            # Shared utilities, AI engines, management commands
│   ├── users/           # Custom User model, preferences, profiles
│   ├── dashboard/       # Main dashboard views
│   ├── journal/         # Daily journaling, mood, gratitude
│   ├── health/          # Weight, vitals, fitness, nutrition, sleep
│   ├── medical/         # Medical records, medications, providers
│   ├── faith/           # Bible reading plans, prayer, devotionals
│   ├── life/            # Goals, tasks, habits, projects
│   ├── purpose/         # Core values, life purpose
│   ├── finance/         # Financial tracking
│   ├── brain_training/  # Cognitive exercises
│   ├── ai/              # AI coaching chat interface
│   ├── admin_console/   # Staff admin tools, ICC, IOCD
│   ├── help/            # Help system, teaching tool
│   ├── scan/            # Document scanning
│   ├── mobile/          # iOS API, HealthKit, push notifications
│   ├── capture/         # Quick capture (inbox)
│   ├── billing/         # Subscription management
│   ├── security/        # MFA, audit logging
│   └── sms/             # SMS delivery
├── templates/           # Global Django templates
├── static/              # CSS, JS, images
├── docs/                # Documentation
└── ios/                 # iOS native wrapper (Xcode project)
```

### Intelligence Engine Layout

All 14 intelligence engines live under `apps/core/`:

| Directory | Engine | Phase |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| `ai_semantics/` | SUE — Semantic Understanding | 1 (Interpretation) |
| `ai_memory/` | SLCME — Context Memory | 1 (Interpretation) |
| `time/` | HTIE — Temporal Intelligence | 1 (Interpretation) |
| `ai_orchestrator/` | UAIO — Orchestrator | 2 (Execution) |
| `ai_state/` | SAE — State Awareness | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_insights/` | PIE — Proactive Insights | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_predictions/` | PRIE — Predictive Intelligence | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_guidance/` | PGE — Proactive Guidance | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_guidance_learning/` | GLOE — Guidance Learning | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_briefing/` | DBE — Daily Briefing | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_weekly_report/` | WIRE — Weekly Reports | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_explain/` | E3 — Evidence & Explainability | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_delivery/` | DNE — Delivery & Notifications | 3 (Post-Execution) |
| `ai_scheduler/` | ISE — Intelligence Scheduler | 3 (Post-Execution) |

### Key Patterns

- **Soft deletes** — Models use `soft_delete()` method, never hard delete
- **Feature flags** — Module-level (`health_enabled`) and sub-feature (`features.health.weight`)
- **Mixins** — `LoginRequiredMixin`, `AdminRequiredMixin`, `HelpContextMixin`
- **Service layer** — Business logic in `services.py`, not in views
- **Fixtures** — JSON fixtures loaded via `load_initial_data.py` management command

### URL Namespace Convention

Each app has its own URL namespace:

```python
app_name = 'health'        # /health/...
app_name = 'journal'       # /journal/...
app_name = 'admin_console'  # /admin-console/...
app_name = 'medical'       # /medical/...
```

> **Note:** The admin console is staff-only (enforced by `AdminRequiredMixin`). All other apps require standard authentication via `LoginRequiredMixin`.

fields.content:
## First Login & Setup

This guide walks administrators through the initial login process and essential configuration steps.

### Accessing the Admin Console

1. Navigate to the WLJ application and log in with your staff account
2. Click the **Admin Console** link in the navigation (visible only to staff users)
3. You will land on the Admin Console Dashboard at `/admin-console/`

### Dashboard Overview

The Admin Console dashboard presents a grid of management tiles:

| Tile | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| User Management | View and manage user accounts |
| Task Management | Manage system tasks and priorities |
| Email Management | Process and manage email communications |
| Intelligence Command Center | Monitor AI engine states and outputs |
| Intelligence Observability | System health metrics and quality scores |
| Admin Guide | This documentation system |
| Data Imports | Import and manage data fixtures |

### Staff Account Requirements

To access the Admin Console, an account must have `is_staff = True` in the Django user model. This is enforced by the `AdminRequiredMixin` on all admin console views.

### Initial Configuration Checklist

- [ ] Verify your staff account has proper permissions
- [ ] Review the Intelligence Command Center for engine status
- [ ] Check the Observability Dashboard for system health
- [ ] Familiarize yourself with the Admin Guide sections
- [ ] Review active users and their onboarding status

### Operational Notes

**Authentication flow:** WLJ uses django-allauth with email-based authentication. There are no usernames — email addresses serve as the unique identifier.

**MFA:** Multi-factor authentication via TOTP is available through the Security module (`apps/security/`). Staff accounts should enable MFA for additional security.

**Session management:** Standard Django session-based authentication for web access. The iOS app uses Bearer token authentication via the mobile API.

> **Important:** The Admin Console is accessible only to users with `is_staff=True`. Regular users will receive a 403 Forbidden response if they attempt to access admin URLs.

fields.content:
## Admin Console Tour

The Admin Console is the central management hub for WLJ. This tour covers each major area and its capabilities.

### Navigation

The Admin Console is located at `/admin-console/` and is accessible from the main navigation bar (visible only to staff users). The dashboard provides tile-based access to all management features.

### User Management

**Path:** Admin Console → User Management

View all registered users, their onboarding status, and account details. Key information includes:

- Email address and registration date
- Onboarding completion status
- Terms acceptance version
- Last login timestamp
- Active coaching persona selection

### Task Management

**Path:** Admin Console → Task Management

Manage the automated task queue that Claude Code uses for system improvements:

- View pending, in-progress, and completed tasks
- Create new improvement tasks with executable descriptions
- Monitor task execution status and outputs
- Recalculate task priorities

### Intelligence Command Center (ICC)

**Path:** Admin Console → Intelligence Command Center

The ICC provides real-time visibility into the AI intelligence system:

- **State View** — Current SAE state snapshots per user
- **Guidance View** — Active guidance items, delivery status, user interactions
- **Prediction View** — Active predictions, confidence scores, accuracy tracking
- **Insight View** — Generated insights, categories, read status

### Intelligence Observability Dashboard (IOCD)

**Path:** Admin Console → Intelligence Observability

System-wide health monitoring:

- Daily metrics snapshots (generated automatically)
- Engine performance trends over 7/14/30 days
- Quality gate pass rates (ICQG)
- Delivery success rates
- Evidence attachment rates

### Data Imports

**Path:** Admin Console → Data Imports

Manage fixture loading and data initialization:

- View `DataLoadConfig` records showing what has been loaded
- Trigger fixture reloads when needed
- Monitor import status and errors

> **Tip:** Bookmark the Admin Console dashboard for quick access. The URL is always `/admin-console/`.

fields.title: Intelligence Command Center Overview
fields.content:
## Intelligence Command Center Overview

The Intelligence Command Center (ICC) is the primary interface for monitoring and managing WLJ's AI intelligence outputs.

### What is the ICC?

The ICC provides a unified view of all intelligence generated by the 14-engine cognitive stack. It allows administrators to:

- Monitor real-time user state across all modules
- Review and manage guidance items generated by PGE
- Track prediction accuracy and confidence from PRIE
- Inspect insights detected by PIE
- View daily briefings and weekly reports

### ICC Panels

#### State & Context Panel
Shows the current SAE (State Awareness Engine) snapshot for each user, including:
- Active module states (health, journal, faith, etc.)
- Recent activity patterns
- Current coaching persona
- Engagement metrics

#### Guidance Management Panel
Displays all PGE-generated guidance with filtering by:
- Status: pending, delivered, acted_on, dismissed
- Priority: critical, high, medium, low
- Module: which life domain the guidance addresses
- Delivery channel: in-app, email, push notification

#### Prediction Management Panel
Shows PRIE predictions with:
- Prediction type and target metric
- Confidence score (0-100%)
- Predicted value vs. actual outcome
- Accuracy tracking over time

### Operational Use

Common administrative tasks in the ICC:

1. **Review guidance quality** — Check that PGE outputs are relevant and actionable
2. **Monitor prediction accuracy** — Ensure PRIE confidence scores correlate with actual outcomes
3. **Inspect user states** — Verify SAE snapshots are updating correctly after user actions
4. **Audit delivery** — Confirm DNE is successfully delivering intelligence to users

### Technical Details

The ICC views are implemented in `apps/admin_console/views.py` and use the following models:

```python
# Key models accessed by ICC
from apps.core.ai_state.models import UserStateSnapshot
from apps.core.ai_guidance.models import ProactiveGuidance
from apps.core.ai_predictions.models import UserPrediction
from apps.core.ai_insights.models import ProactiveInsight
from apps.core.ai_briefing.models import DailyBriefing
```

All ICC views require staff access via `AdminRequiredMixin` and provide `HelpContextMixin` for integrated help.

> **Note:** The ICC is read-only for most operations. Guidance and prediction management actions (dismiss, acknowledge) are performed through the user-facing interfaces.

fields.description: The three-phase intelligence pipeline, engine inventory, and execution flow.

fields.title: Three-Phase Intelligence Pipeline
fields.content:
## Three-Phase Intelligence Pipeline

Every intelligence operation in WLJ flows through three strictly separated phases. This architecture ensures safety, consistency, and auditability.

### Phase 1 — Interpretation

**Purpose:** Understand user meaning safely and accurately. Prepare execution instructions.

**Engines:**
- **SUE** (Semantic Understanding Engine) — Parses user intent, extracts entities, detects ambiguity
- **SLCME** (Self-Learning Context Memory) — Resolves context references using learned mappings
- **HTIE** (Human Temporal Intelligence) — Converts natural language time expressions to timestamps

**Key rule:** Phase 1 engines do NOT execute actions. They only prepare interpretation data.

### Phase 2 — Execution

**Purpose:** Execute actions safely with single authority.

**Engine:**
- **UAIO** (Unified AI Orchestrator) — The sole execution authority in the system

UAIO receives interpreted instructions from Phase 1 and routes them to appropriate domain action handlers. No other engine may execute actions independently.

### Phase 3 — Post-Execution

**Purpose:** Update awareness, detect patterns, predict trajectory, surface guidance.

**Engines (in execution order):**

| Order | Engine | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------|
| 1 | SAE | Update user state snapshot |
| 2 | PIE | Detect patterns, generate insights |
| 3 | PRIE | Project future trajectories |
| 4 | PGE (+ICQG, +E3) | Generate evidence-based guidance |
| 5 | GLOE | Learn from guidance interactions |
| 6 | DBE (+ICQG, +E3) | Compile daily briefings |
| 7 | WIRE (+ICQG, +E3) | Generate weekly reports |
| 8 | DNE (+ICQG) | Deliver outputs to users |

**Cross-cutting:** ISE (Scheduler) orchestrates when engines run. ICQG (Quality Gate) filters outputs before storage/delivery.

### Pipeline Diagram

```
User Input
  → Phase 1: SUE → SLCME → HTIE
    → Phase 2: UAIO (execute action)
      → Phase 3: SAE → PIE → PRIE → PGE → GLOE → DBE → WIRE → DNE
  → Response to user
```

### Phase Boundary Rules

1. **No execution in Phase 1** — Interpretation engines must never trigger side effects
2. **Single execution authority** — Only UAIO may execute domain actions
3. **No execution in Phase 3** — Post-execution engines observe and generate, never act
4. **Sequential within Phase 3** — SAE must complete before PIE, PIE before PRIE, etc.

> **Architectural authority:** These phase boundaries are defined in `docs/INTELLIGENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md` and must never be violated. If existing code violates them, it must be refactored to comply.

fields.title: Engine Inventory
fields.content:
## Engine Inventory

WLJ's cognitive stack consists of 14 intelligence engines plus one cross-cutting quality layer. Each engine has a specific responsibility and belongs to exactly one execution phase.

### Phase 1 — Interpretation Engines

#### SUE — Semantic Understanding Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_semantics/`
- **Purpose:** Parse human intent, extract entities, detect ambiguity in user input
- **Key capability:** Converts natural language into structured action instructions

#### SLCME — Self-Learning Context Memory Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_memory/`
- **Purpose:** Remember and reuse context resolutions from previous interactions
- **Key capability:** Auto-applies learned mappings with confidence scoring

#### HTIE — Human Temporal Intelligence Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/time/`
- **Purpose:** Resolve human time expressions ("yesterday", "last Tuesday") to precise timestamps
- **Key capability:** Handles relative, absolute, and fuzzy time references

### Phase 2 — Execution Engine

#### UAIO — Unified AI Orchestrator
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_orchestrator/`
- **Purpose:** Central brain connecting all engines to the AI pipeline
- **Key capability:** Routes interpreted instructions to domain-specific action handlers
- **Authority:** UAIO is the ONLY engine that may execute actions

### Phase 3 — Post-Execution Engines

#### SAE — State Awareness Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_state/`
- **Purpose:** Maintain authoritative user state snapshot
- **Key capability:** Persistent state that reflects current user condition across all modules

#### PIE — Proactive Insight Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_insights/`
- **Purpose:** Detect patterns and generate factual insights
- **Key capability:** Event-driven + scheduled insight detection using configurable rules

#### PRIE — Predictive Intelligence Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_predictions/`
- **Purpose:** Project future trajectories using statistical methods
- **Key capability:** Linear regression predictions with confidence scoring

#### PGE — Proactive Guidance Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_guidance/`
- **Purpose:** Surface evidence-based proactive guidance
- **Key capability:** Generates actionable recommendations from state, insights, and predictions

#### GLOE — Guidance Learning Optimization Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_guidance_learning/`
- **Purpose:** Learn from user guidance interactions
- **Key capability:** Tracks engagement patterns to improve PGE ranking

#### DBE — Daily Briefing Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_briefing/`
- **Purpose:** Aggregate daily intelligence summaries
- **Key capability:** Compiles insights, predictions, and guidance into a coherent daily brief

#### WIRE — Weekly Intelligence Report Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_weekly_report/`
- **Purpose:** Generate weekly longitudinal summaries
- **Key capability:** Trend analysis across 7-day windows

#### E3 — Evidence & Explainability Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_explain/`
- **Purpose:** Attach evidence and explanations to intelligence outputs
- **Key capability:** Non-blocking enrichment of PGE, DBE, and WIRE outputs

#### DNE — Delivery & Notification Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_delivery/`
- **Purpose:** Deliver intelligence through configured channels
- **Key capability:** In-app, email, SMS, and push notification delivery with throttling and deduplication

#### ISE — Intelligence Scheduler Engine
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_scheduler/`
- **Purpose:** Centrally manage scheduled execution of all engines
- **Key capability:** Cron-triggered every 5 minutes, coordinates engine timing

### Cross-Cutting Quality Layer

#### ICQG — Intelligence Calibration & Quality Gate
- **Location:** `apps/core/ai_quality/`
- **Purpose:** Ensure output quality and reduce noise
- **Key capability:** 72-hour suppression of repeated guidance, conflict detection, minimum quality thresholds
- **Integration points:** Hooks into PGE, DBE, WIRE, and DNE; always fails open

fields.title: Execution Flow
fields.content:
## Execution Flow

This article traces a complete intelligence execution from user input through all three phases to response delivery.

### Example: User Logs Weight

When a user logs a weight entry, the following sequence executes:

#### Step 1: User Input
User enters "185 lbs" in the weight tracking form and submits.

#### Step 2: Phase 1 — Interpretation

```
SUE: Parses intent as "log_weight" with entity {value: 185, unit: "lbs"}
SLCME: No context resolution needed (direct numeric input)
HTIE: Resolves timestamp to current datetime (no time expression provided)
```

**Output:** Structured action instruction: `{action: 'log_weight', value: 185, unit: 'lbs', timestamp: '2026-02-15T10:30:00Z'}`

#### Step 3: Phase 2 — Execution

```
UAIO: Routes to health.weight action handler
  → Creates WeightEntry(value=185, unit='lbs', logged_at=timestamp)
  → Returns success confirmation
```

#### Step 4: Phase 3 — Post-Execution

```
SAE: Updates user state snapshot
  → current_weight = 185
  → weight_trend = "decreasing" (was 187 last week)
  → last_weight_entry = today

PIE: Evaluates insight rules
  → Rule: "weight_streak_3" → User has logged weight 3 days in a row
  → Rule: "weight_milestone" → User crossed 185 threshold
  → Generates InsightEvent for each triggered rule

PRIE: Updates predictions
  → Recalculates linear regression for weight trajectory
  → Prediction: "At current rate, will reach 180 by March 15"
  → Confidence: 72%

PGE: Evaluates guidance rules
  → Rule: "weight_on_track" → Generates encouraging guidance
  → ICQG filters: checks for 72h suppression, deduplication
  → E3 enriches: attaches evidence (3-week trend data)

DBE: Queues for daily briefing compilation
DNE: Queues guidance for delivery via configured channels
```

### Scheduling vs. Event-Driven

Not all Phase 3 engines run on every user action:

| Engine | Trigger | Frequency |
|--------|---------|----------|
| SAE | Every action | Immediate |
| PIE | Every action + scheduled | Immediate + daily scan |
| PRIE | Every action + scheduled | Immediate + daily recalculation |
| PGE | Scheduled | Every ISE cycle (5 min) |
| GLOE | User interaction | On guidance response |
| DBE | Scheduled | Daily (morning) |
| WIRE | Scheduled | Weekly (Sunday) |
| DNE | Scheduled | Every 10 minutes |
| ISE | Cron | Every 5 minutes |

### Error Handling

The pipeline is designed to be resilient:

- Each engine runs independently with try/except wrapping
- A failure in PIE does not prevent PRIE from running
- ICQG always **fails open** — if quality checks fail, the output passes through
- DNE retries failed deliveries on the next cycle

> **Key principle:** The pipeline never blocks the user response. Phase 3 engines run asynchronously after the user receives confirmation of their action.

fields.title: Intelligence Engines — Interpretation
fields.description: Deep dive into Phase 1 engines (SUE, SLCME, HTIE) and the Phase 2 orchestrator (UAIO).

fields.title: SUE: Semantic Understanding Engine
fields.content:
## SUE: Semantic Understanding Engine

**Phase:** 1 (Interpretation)  
**Location:** `apps/core/ai_semantics/`  
**Purpose:** Parse human intent, extract entities, and detect ambiguity in user input.

### Conceptual Overview

SUE is the first engine in the intelligence pipeline. It takes raw user input (natural language from the AI assistant chat) and converts it into structured action instructions that UAIO can execute.

SUE handles three core tasks:

1. **Intent Classification** — What does the user want to do? (e.g., log weight, create journal entry, set reminder)
2. **Entity Extraction** — What are the key data points? (e.g., weight value, date, mood rating)
3. **Ambiguity Detection** — Is the input unclear enough to require clarification?

### How SUE Works

SUE uses the OpenAI API with carefully crafted system prompts to perform semantic analysis:

```
User: "I walked 3 miles yesterday morning"

SUE Output:
{
  "intent": "log_fitness",
  "entities": {
    "activity": "walking",
    "distance": 3,
    "unit": "miles",
    "time_expression": "yesterday morning"
  },
  "confidence": 0.95,
  "ambiguity": null
}
```

When ambiguity is detected, SUE returns a clarification request instead of an action instruction:

```
User: "Log my reading"

SUE Output:
{
  "intent": "ambiguous",
  "candidates": ["log_bible_reading", "log_book_reading"],
  "clarification_needed": "Which type of reading?"
}
```

### Operational Perspective

SUE runs automatically as part of every AI assistant conversation. Administrators can monitor SUE behavior through:

- **AI Chat Logs** — View parsed intents and entity extractions
- **Ambiguity Rate** — Track how often clarification is needed (lower is better)
- **Intent Distribution** — See which actions users request most frequently

### Technical Details

**Key files:**
- `apps/core/ai_semantics/services.py` — Main semantic parsing service
- `apps/core/ai_semantics/prompts.py` — System prompts for intent classification

**Integration with SLCME:** When SUE detects ambiguity, SLCME is consulted to see if a previous clarification has been learned. If SLCME has a high-confidence mapping, the ambiguity is automatically resolved without asking the user.

**Integration with HTIE:** When SUE extracts time expressions ("yesterday", "last Tuesday at 3pm"), HTIE converts them to precise timestamps before passing to UAIO.

> **Phase boundary:** SUE must NEVER execute actions. It only produces structured interpretation data for UAIO.

fields.title: SLCME: Self-Learning Context Memory Engine
fields.content:
## SLCME: Self-Learning Context Memory Engine

**Phase:** 1 (Interpretation)  
**Location:** `apps/core/ai_memory/`  
**Purpose:** Learn from user clarifications and automatically reuse context resolutions.

### Conceptual Overview

SLCME solves a fundamental UX problem: users shouldn't have to clarify the same ambiguous input twice. When SUE detects ambiguity and the user provides a clarification, SLCME stores that resolution as a learned mapping. On future similar inputs, SLCME applies the learned mapping automatically.

### Learning Flow

```
1. User says: "Log my reading"
2. SUE detects ambiguity: could be Bible or book reading
3. System asks: "Which type of reading?"
4. User clarifies: "Bible reading"
5. SLCME stores: {"log my reading" → "log_bible_reading", confidence: 0.8}

Next time:
1. User says: "Log my reading"
2. SUE detects same ambiguity
3. SLCME resolves automatically: "log_bible_reading" (confidence: 0.8)
4. No clarification needed!
```

### Confidence Scoring

SLCME uses confidence scores to decide whether to auto-apply a learned mapping:

| Confidence | Behavior |
|-----------|----------|
| 0.0 - 0.5 | Do not auto-apply; still ask for clarification |
| 0.5 - 0.8 | Auto-apply but mention it to user ("I assumed you meant...") |
| 0.8 - 1.0 | Auto-apply silently |

Confidence increases with each consistent use and decreases if the user ever overrides the mapping.

### Operational Perspective

Administrators can view learned mappings through the Admin Console:

- **Memory entries per user** — How many context resolutions each user has
- **Override rate** — How often users override auto-applied mappings
- **Confidence distribution** — Overall confidence health of learned mappings

### Technical Details

**Key files:**
- `apps/core/ai_memory/models.py` — `ContextMemory` model storing learned mappings
- `apps/core/ai_memory/services.py` — Lookup and learning service

**Model fields:**
```python
class ContextMemory(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    input_pattern = models.TextField()  # The ambiguous input
    resolved_intent = models.CharField()  # What it resolved to
    confidence = models.FloatField()  # Auto-apply threshold
    use_count = models.IntegerField()  # Times used
    last_used = models.DateTimeField()
```

**Decay mechanism:** Mappings that haven't been used in 90 days have their confidence reduced by 0.1 per month, ensuring stale mappings don't persist indefinitely.

> **Phase boundary:** SLCME must NEVER execute actions. It only provides context resolution data to SUE and UAIO.

fields.title: HTIE: Human Temporal Intelligence Engine
fields.content:
## HTIE: Human Temporal Intelligence Engine

**Phase:** 1 (Interpretation)  
**Location:** `apps/core/time/`  
**Purpose:** Convert natural language time expressions to precise timestamps.

### Conceptual Overview

Humans express time in imprecise, context-dependent ways: "yesterday", "last Tuesday", "this morning", "a couple weeks ago". HTIE resolves these expressions to exact timestamps that the system can use for data logging, querying, and analysis.

### Time Resolution Examples

| User Input | HTIE Resolution | Context |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| "yesterday" | 2026-02-14 | Relative to current date |
| "last Tuesday" | 2026-02-11 | Most recent Tuesday |
| "this morning" | 2026-02-15T08:00:00 | Morning of current day |
| "3pm" | 2026-02-15T15:00:00 | Today at specified time |
| "two weeks ago" | 2026-02-01 | Relative calculation |
| "January 5th" | 2026-01-05 | Specific date, current year |
| "yesterday at 3pm" | 2026-02-14T15:00:00 | Combined relative + absolute |

### User Timezone Handling

HTIE always considers the user's configured timezone (stored in `UserPreferences.timezone`):

```python
# HTIE uses user's timezone for all resolutions
user_tz = user.preferences.timezone  # e.g., 'America/New_York'
now_in_user_tz = timezone.now().astimezone(user_tz)
```

This ensures that "yesterday" always means yesterday in the user's local time, not server time.

### Integration with the AI Assistant

When the AI assistant processes user input, HTIE is invoked after SUE extracts time expressions:

```
User: "I slept 7 hours last night"

SUE extracts: time_expression = "last night"
HTIE resolves: sleep_start = 2026-02-14T22:00:00, sleep_end = 2026-02-15T05:00:00
UAIO uses: Creates SleepEntry with resolved timestamps
```

### Edge Cases

HTIE handles several tricky scenarios:

- **Ambiguous dates:** "next Friday" — resolved based on whether today IS Friday
- **Year boundaries:** "last December" in January resolves to previous year
- **Missing specifics:** "morning" defaults to 8:00 AM in user's timezone
- **Duration expressions:** "for 2 hours" calculates end time from start

### Operational Perspective

HTIE operates transparently — users rarely notice it working. Monitor for:

- **Resolution accuracy** — Are timestamps correct for the user's intent?
- **Timezone issues** — Users with incorrect timezone settings may see wrong dates
- **Failed resolutions** — Expressions HTIE couldn't parse (falls back to current time)

### Technical Details

**Key files:**
- `apps/core/time/services.py` — Time resolution service
- `apps/core/time/parsers.py` — Natural language time parsers

The system prompt for the AI assistant always includes the user's current time, ensuring HTIE has the correct reference point for relative time calculations.

> **Phase boundary:** HTIE must NEVER execute actions. It only provides timestamp resolution data.

fields.title: UAIO: Unified AI Orchestrator
fields.content:
## UAIO: Unified AI Orchestrator

**Phase:** 2 (Execution)  
**Location:** `apps/core/ai_orchestrator/`  
**Purpose:** Central execution authority connecting all engines to the AI pipeline.

### Conceptual Overview

UAIO is the brain of the WLJ intelligence system. It is the **sole execution authority** — no other engine may execute domain actions independently. UAIO receives interpreted instructions from Phase 1 (SUE + SLCME + HTIE) and routes them to the appropriate domain action handler.

### Execution Flow

```
Phase 1 Output (interpreted instruction)
  ↓
UAIO validates instruction
  ↓
UAIO selects action handler
  ↓
Action handler executes domain logic
  ↓
UAIO returns result
  ↓
Phase 3 engines process post-execution
```

### Action Handlers

UAIO maintains a registry of domain action handlers, each responsible for a specific type of action:

| Handler | Domain | Example Actions |
|---------|--------|-----------------|
| Health Handler | `apps/health/` | Log weight, record vitals, log workout |
| Journal Handler | `apps/journal/` | Create entry, update mood, add gratitude |
| Faith Handler | `apps/faith/` | Log reading, record prayer, mark devotional |
| Life Handler | `apps/life/` | Create task, update goal, log habit |
| Medical Handler | `apps/medical/` | Add medication, record appointment |

### Validation

Before executing, UAIO validates:

1. **Intent is recognized** — The action type maps to a known handler
2. **Required entities present** — All mandatory fields are provided
3. **User has permission** — The user can perform this action
4. **Data is valid** — Values are within acceptable ranges

If validation fails, UAIO returns an error without executing.

### Operational Perspective

UAIO operations can be monitored through:

- **Action success rate** — Percentage of instructions that execute successfully
- **Handler distribution** — Which domains receive the most actions
- **Validation failures** — Common reasons instructions are rejected
- **Execution time** — How long actions take to complete

### Technical Details

**Key files:**
- `apps/core/ai_orchestrator/services.py` — Main orchestrator service
- `apps/core/ai_orchestrator/handlers/` — Domain-specific action handlers

**Orchestrator service pattern:**
```python
class UAIOService:
    def execute(self, user, interpreted_instruction):
        # 1. Validate instruction
        handler = self.get_handler(instruction.intent)
        if not handler:
            raise UnknownIntentError(instruction.intent)
        
        # 2. Execute via handler
        result = handler.execute(user, instruction.entities)
        
        # 3. Trigger Phase 3 post-execution
        self.trigger_post_execution(user, result)
        
        return result
```

### Safety Guarantees

UAIO enforces critical safety rules:

- **No cascading execution** — An action handler cannot trigger another action
- **Atomic operations** — Actions either complete fully or roll back
- **Audit trail** — Every execution is logged for accountability
- **Rate limiting** — Prevents runaway execution from malformed input

> **Architectural authority:** UAIO is the ONLY execution authority. If any code attempts to execute domain actions outside UAIO, it must be refactored to route through the orchestrator.

fields.title: Intelligence Lifecycle
fields.description: How intelligence flows from state through insights, predictions, and guidance.

fields.title: State → Insight → Prediction → Guidance
fields.content:
## State → Insight → Prediction → Guidance

The intelligence lifecycle follows a natural progression from raw data to actionable recommendations.

### The Four Stages

#### 1. State (SAE)

**What:** An authoritative snapshot of the user's current condition across all modules.

```json
{
  "health": {
    "current_weight": 185,
    "weight_trend": "decreasing",
    "last_workout": "2026-02-14",
    "sleep_avg_7d": 7.2
  },
  "journal": {
    "entries_this_week": 4,
    "avg_mood": 7.5,
    "streak": 12
  },
  "faith": {
    "reading_plan_progress": 0.65,
    "days_since_prayer": 0
  }
}
```

State is rebuilt after every user action and serves as the foundation for all downstream intelligence.

#### 2. Insight (PIE)

**What:** Factual observations detected by evaluating patterns in state data.

Insights answer "What happened?" — they are observations, not recommendations:

- "You've logged weight 7 days in a row" (streak detection)
- "Your sleep average dropped 1.2 hours this week" (trend detection)
- "You completed 80% of your reading plan" (milestone detection)

PIE uses configurable **insight rules** that evaluate conditions against the current state.

#### 3. Prediction (PRIE)

**What:** Statistical projections of where the user is heading based on current trajectory.

Predictions answer "What will happen?":

- "At current rate, you'll reach 180 lbs by March 15" (trajectory projection)
- "Sleep trend suggests 6.5 hours average by next week" (declining metric)
- "Journal streak likely to reach 30 days" (positive momentum)

PRIE uses linear regression on historical data points to calculate predictions with confidence scores.

#### 4. Guidance (PGE)

**What:** Evidence-based recommendations that help the user act on their intelligence.

Guidance answers "What should I do?":

- "Consider a rest day — you've worked out 5 days straight" (overtraining prevention)
- "Your weight is on track! Keep logging to maintain momentum" (positive reinforcement)
- "Try journaling about your sleep patterns — mood and sleep appear correlated" (cross-domain connection)

PGE generates guidance from configurable **guidance rules** that consider state, insights, and predictions together.

### The Cascade

```
User Action
  → SAE updates state
    → PIE evaluates insight rules against new state
      → PRIE recalculates predictions using updated data
        → PGE evaluates guidance rules using state + insights + predictions
          → ICQG filters for quality/deduplication
            → E3 attaches evidence and explanations
              → DNE delivers to user via configured channels
```

Each stage builds on the previous one, creating increasingly actionable intelligence.

> **Key insight:** The power of this cascade is that it connects dots across domains. A sleep decline (SAE state) triggers an insight (PIE), which influences a mood prediction (PRIE), which generates guidance about journaling before bed (PGE).

fields.title: Engine Communication Patterns
fields.content:
## Engine Communication Patterns

The 14 intelligence engines communicate through well-defined patterns to ensure consistency and maintainability.

### Direct Invocation

Most engine communication follows a direct service-call pattern:

```python
# Phase 3 post-execution sequence
from apps.core.ai_state.services import update_state
from apps.core.ai_insights.services import evaluate_insights
from apps.core.ai_predictions.services import update_predictions

# Sequential execution
state = update_state(user)          # SAE
insights = evaluate_insights(user)  # PIE
predictions = update_predictions(user)  # PRIE
```

The calling code ensures engines execute in the correct order within Phase 3.

### Event-Driven Communication

Some engines respond to events rather than direct invocation:

| Event | Source | Listener |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Weight logged | Health module | PIE (insight rules), PRIE (recalculate) |
| Guidance interacted | User | GLOE (learn from response) |
| Insight generated | PIE | PGE (may trigger guidance) |
| Daily schedule tick | ISE | DBE (compile briefing) |
| Weekly schedule tick | ISE | WIRE (compile report) |

### Shared Data Contracts

Engines communicate through shared models and data structures:

#### State Contract (SAE → PIE, PRIE, PGE)
```python
# UserStateSnapshot provides the common data contract
class UserStateSnapshot:
    user: User
    health_state: dict   # Weight, vitals, fitness, sleep
    journal_state: dict  # Entries, mood, streaks
    faith_state: dict    # Reading plans, prayer
    life_state: dict     # Tasks, goals, habits
    updated_at: datetime
```

#### Insight Contract (PIE → PGE, DBE)
```python
# ProactiveInsight provides insight data
class ProactiveInsight:
    user: User
    rule_key: str        # Which rule generated it
    category: str        # health, journal, faith, etc.
    title: str           # Human-readable summary
    evidence: dict       # Supporting data points
    created_at: datetime
```

#### Prediction Contract (PRIE → PGE, DBE)
```python
# UserPrediction provides prediction data
class UserPrediction:
    user: User
    metric: str          # What's being predicted
    predicted_value: float
    confidence: float    # 0.0 to 1.0
    target_date: date
    created_at: datetime
```

### Quality Gate Integration

ICQG hooks into the pipeline at specific points:

```
PGE generates guidance candidate
  → ICQG checks: duplicate? (72h window)
  → ICQG checks: conflicting guidance?
  → ICQG checks: minimum quality score?
  → If passes: store and enrich via E3
  → If fails: discard (logged for monitoring)
  → If ICQG errors: fail open (pass through)
```

### ISE Coordination

ISE runs every 5 minutes and coordinates which engines execute:

```python
# ISE schedule registry
SCHEDULE = {
    'pge_evaluate': {'interval': '5m'},
    'dbe_compile': {'interval': '24h', 'time': '06:00'},
    'wire_compile': {'interval': '7d', 'day': 'sunday'},
    'dne_deliver': {'interval': '10m'},
}
```

> **Important:** Engines must never call each other directly outside the defined patterns. All cross-engine communication should go through the established contracts.

fields.title: Data Flow & Dependencies
fields.content:
## Data Flow & Dependencies

Understanding how data flows between engines and modules is critical for troubleshooting and extension.

### Module → Engine Data Flow

Each application module feeds data into the intelligence pipeline:

| Module | Data Created | Engines Consuming |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|
| Health | WeightEntry, SleepEntry, WorkoutSession | SAE, PIE, PRIE |
| Journal | JournalEntry, MoodRating | SAE, PIE, PRIE |
| Faith | ReadingProgress, PrayerEntry | SAE, PIE |
| Life | Task, Goal, HabitLog | SAE, PIE, PRIE |
| Medical | Medication, LabResult | SAE, PIE |
| Finance | BudgetEntry | SAE, PIE |

### Engine Dependency Graph

```
SAE (state)
  │
  ├─→ PIE (insights) ────┐
  │                        │
  ├─→ PRIE (predictions) ─┤
  │                        │
  └───────────────────────┤
                            │
                     PGE (guidance)
                            │
                     ICQG (quality filter)
                            │
                     E3 (evidence enrichment)
                            │
                  ┌────────┼────────┐
                  │        │        │
                 DBE     WIRE     DNE
              (daily)  (weekly) (deliver)
```

### Data Retention

Different data types have different retention characteristics:

| Data Type | Retention | Managed By |
|-----------|-----------|------------|
| User state snapshots | Current only (overwritten) | SAE |
| Insights | 90 days | PIE with archival |
| Predictions | Until resolved or expired | PRIE |
| Guidance | Indefinite (soft deleted) | PGE |
| Daily briefings | 30 days | DBE |
| Weekly reports | 90 days | WIRE |
| Delivery records | 30 days | DNE |
| Metrics snapshots | 90 days | IOCD |

### Adding New Data Sources

When a new module or feature creates data that should feed into intelligence:

1. **Fire SAE state update** — Call `update_state(user)` after data creation
2. **Add PIE insight rules** — Create rules in `apps/core/ai_insights/rules/`
3. **Add PRIE prediction rules** — Create rules in `apps/core/ai_predictions/rules/`
4. **Add PGE guidance rules** — Create rules in `apps/core/ai_guidance/rules/`
5. **Update SAE snapshot builder** — Add new module state to the snapshot

See `docs/ENGINE_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md` for the complete step-by-step integration pattern.

### Cross-Module Intelligence

One of WLJ's key strengths is cross-module intelligence. Because SAE maintains state across all modules, PIE and PGE can detect patterns that span domains:

**Example cross-module insight:**
```
PIE detects: Sleep quality drops when no journal entry is written
Evidence: 80% correlation over 30 days
PGE generates: "Consider journaling before bed — your sleep quality 
               tends to be better on days you write."
```

This is only possible because the intelligence pipeline has unified access to all module data through SAE.

> **Key principle:** Data should flow downhill through the pipeline. Modules create data, SAE aggregates it, PIE/PRIE analyze it, PGE acts on it. Data should never flow uphill (e.g., PGE should never write to a module's models).

fields.title: Coaching Personas
fields.description: How WLJ adapts its AI personality, tone, and communication style to match each user's preference through database-driven coaching styles.

fields.title: Persona Selection & Adaptation
fields.content:
# Persona Selection & Adaptation

## Conceptual Overview

Whole Life Journey does not use a single AI voice. Instead, every user selects a **coaching style** (also called a persona) that controls the tone, vocabulary, and emotional register of every AI-generated response they receive. The system ships with eight personas out of the box, and administrators can add, edit, or disable personas at any time through the Django admin — no code deploys required.

The underlying principle is **relational trust**: users engage more deeply with an AI that speaks in a way they find comfortable. A user who thrives on tough love picks the Army Drill Sergeant; a user who needs gentle encouragement picks the Gentle Guide. The data and intelligence are identical — only the delivery wrapper changes.

### Built-In Personas

| Key | Name | Icon | Category | Description |
|-----|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `gentle` | Gentle Guide | 🌱 | General | Soft, nurturing, patient. Extra grace and self-compassion. |
| `supportive` | Supportive Partner | 🤝 | General | Warm, balanced, like a trusted friend. **(Default)** |
| `direct` | Direct Coach | 🎯 | General | Clear, straightforward, action-oriented. No sugarcoating. |
| `southern_belle` | Southern Belle | 🌺 | General | Warm Southern charm with a steel backbone. |
| `texas_rancher` | Texas Rancher | 🤠 | General | Straight-shooting wisdom, hard work values. |
| `new_york` | New York Straight-Talker | 🗽 | General | Fast-paced, no-nonsense. Tough love with heart. |
| `california_chill` | California Chill | 🏄 | General | Laid-back vibes with mindful wisdom. |
| `drill_sergeant` | Army Drill Sergeant | 🎖️ | Armed Forces | No excuses, no shortcuts. Military intensity. |

---

## Operational Guide

### How Users Select a Persona

Users choose their coaching style during **onboarding** (Step 4 of the wizard) and can change it anytime from **Settings > AI Preferences**. The selection is stored on `UserPreferences.ai_coaching_style` as a slug key (e.g., `"supportive"`, `"drill_sergeant"`).

### How Persona Affects AI Output

Every time the AI generates a response — whether a chat reply, a dashboard insight, a daily briefing summary, or a proactive check-in — the system:

1. Reads the user’s `ai_coaching_style` from their preferences.
2. Loads the corresponding `CoachingStyle` record from the database (with 1-hour cache).
3. Appends the persona’s `prompt_instructions` to the system prompt sent to OpenAI.

The persona instructions tell the AI *how* to communicate. For example, the Supportive Partner says:

> *"Be warm but balanced — like a trusted friend walking alongside them. Use phrases like 'I noticed...', 'you might consider...'. Balance accountability with encouragement."*

While the Direct Coach says:

> *"Be clear, straightforward, and action-oriented. Don’t sugarcoat. Use direct language: 'Do this', 'You need to...'. Keep it brief and punchy."*

### Managing Personas in Admin

Navigate to **Django Admin > AI > Coaching Styles** to manage personas.

**Adding a New Persona:**

1. Click **Add Coaching Style**.
2. Fill in the required fields:
   - `key`: Unique slug (e.g., `midwest_neighbor`). Cannot be changed after users select it.
   - `name`: Display name shown in the UI.
   - `description`: Brief description shown during selection (max 300 chars).
   - `icon`: Single emoji for UI display.
   - `prompt_instructions`: The full AI behavioral instructions. This is the most important field.
   - `category`: Group for UI display (General or Armed Forces). Add new categories by updating `CATEGORY_CHOICES` in the model.
   - `sort_order`: Controls display position in the selection UI.
3. Set `is_active = True` to make it available.
4. Save. The cache clears automatically.

**Disabling a Persona:**

Set `is_active = False`. Users currently using that persona will automatically fall back to the default persona (the one with `is_default = True`). The fallback chain is:

1. User’s selected style (if active)
2. The default style (`is_default = True`)
3. Any active style (ultimate fallback)

> **Important:** Never delete a CoachingStyle record if users have selected it. Disable it instead. The `ai_coaching_style` field on UserPreferences stores the key, and orphaned keys gracefully fall back.

### Cache Behavior

Coaching styles are cached for 1 hour with the following keys:

- `coaching_styles_all` — all active styles list
- `coaching_styles_by_category` — grouped by category
- `coaching_style_{key}` — individual style lookup
- `system_prompt_{style}_{faith}` — composed system prompts

All caches **automatically invalidate** when any `CoachingStyle` record is saved. No manual cache clearing is needed.

---

## Technical Reference

### Model: `CoachingStyle`

**Location:** `apps/ai/models.py`
**Table:** `ai_coachingstyle`

```python
class CoachingStyle(models.Model):
    key = models.SlugField(max_length=50, unique=True)
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    description = models.CharField(max_length=300)
    icon = models.CharField(max_length=10, default="\ud83e\udd1d")
    category = models.CharField(max_length=50, blank=True, choices=CATEGORY_CHOICES)
    prompt_instructions = models.TextField()
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    is_default = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    sort_order = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)
```

**Key methods:**

- `CoachingStyle.get_active_styles()` — Returns all active styles (cached 1 hour).
- `CoachingStyle.get_by_key(key)` — Lookup with fallback chain.
- `CoachingStyle.get_styles_by_category()` — Grouped for template display.
- `CoachingStyle.get_choices()` — Returns `(key, name)` tuples for form fields.

### User Preference Field

**Location:** `apps/users/models.py`

```python
class UserPreferences(models.Model):
    ai_coaching_style = models.CharField(max_length=50, default='supportive')
```

### System Prompt Integration

**Location:** `apps/ai/personal_assistant.py`

The `PersonalAssistant` class builds the system prompt by:

1. Loading `PERSONAL_ASSISTANT_BASE_PROMPT` (identity, behavior rules, response philosophy).
2. Loading the user’s `CoachingStyle.prompt_instructions`.
3. Optionally adding faith context if the user has faith features enabled.
4. Caching the composed prompt with key `system_prompt_{style}_{faith_enabled}`.

### Fixture

**Location:** `apps/ai/fixtures/coaching_styles.json`

Loaded automatically on deploy via `load_initial_data`. Contains all eight built-in personas.

### Key Code Paths

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `apps/ai/models.py` | CoachingStyle model, cache invalidation, fallback logic |
| `apps/ai/fixtures/coaching_styles.json` | Fixture data for built-in personas |
| `apps/ai/personal_assistant.py` | System prompt composition using persona |
| `apps/users/models.py` | `ai_coaching_style` preference field |
| `apps/users/views.py` | Settings view for coaching style selection |
| `apps/users/forms.py` | Form field for coaching style dropdown |

fields.title: Tone Intensity Configuration
fields.content:
# Tone Intensity Configuration

## Conceptual Overview

Beyond selecting a coaching persona, WLJ provides granular control over how the AI communicates through the **AI Prompt Configuration** system. This system allows administrators to fine-tune tone, response length, guidance style, and things to avoid for every type of AI output the system produces.

The design philosophy is **separation of concerns**: the coaching style controls *who* the AI is (personality), while prompt configurations control *what* the AI says and *how much* it says for each specific context (dashboard insights, journal reflections, health encouragement, etc.).

### Prompt Types

Each prompt type represents a distinct AI output context:

| Prompt Type | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `system_base` | Core system prompt (identity + rules) |
| `daily_insight` | Dashboard daily insight card |
| `weekly_summary` | Weekly journal summary |
| `journal_reflection` | Reflection on a specific journal entry |
| `goal_progress` | Goal progress feedback |
| `health_encouragement` | Health module encouragement |
| `glucose_insight` | Blood glucose analysis |
| `prayer_encouragement` | Prayer and faith encouragement |
| `accountability_nudge` | Accountability nudge messages |
| `celebration` | Celebration and positive reinforcement |
| `faith_context` | Faith-specific additions to prompts |
| `journal_home` | Journal home page insight |
| `faith_home` | Faith home page insight |
| `health_home` | Health home page insight |
| `life_home` | Life/Organize home page insight |
| `purpose_home` | Purpose home page insight |
| `capture_summarization` | Audio capture summarization |

---

## Operational Guide

### Configuring Prompt Intensity

Navigate to **Django Admin > AI > AI Prompt Configurations** to manage tone settings.

Each configuration record has the following controls:

**Response Length:**

- `min_sentences` — Minimum sentences in the AI response (default: 2)
- `max_sentences` — Maximum sentences (default: 4)
- `max_tokens` — Hard cap on API response tokens (default: 150)

These controls prevent the AI from being too terse or too verbose. For mobile-friendly contexts, keep max_sentences at 3–4. For detailed analysis views, you can increase to 6–8.

**Tone Guidance:**

The `tone_guidance` field provides additional tone instructions that are appended to the prompt. Examples:

- *"Be warm but not preachy. Never use the word 'should.'"*
- *"Lead with data, follow with encouragement. No motivational platitudes."*
- *"Keep it clinical and factual for health metrics. Skip emotional language."*

**Things to Avoid:**

The `things_to_avoid` field lists explicit prohibitions. These are prefixed with **"IMPORTANT - Avoid:"** in the composed prompt. Examples:

- *"Never shame the user for missing goals."*
- *"Never provide medical advice or diagnoses."*
- *"Never reference specific calorie targets without user data."*

**Example Responses:**

The `example_responses` field provides few-shot examples. While not always sent to the API (due to token constraints), they serve as a reference for administrators writing prompt instructions.

### Refresh Frequency

Each prompt type has a configurable refresh frequency that controls how often cached insights are regenerated:

| Frequency | Behavior |
|-----------|----------|
| `daily` | Regenerate once per day |
| `twice_daily` | Regenerate every 12 hours |
| `three_times_daily` | Regenerate every 8 hours |
| `four_times_daily` | Regenerate every 6 hours |
| `on_data_change` | Regenerate when user logs new data |
| `daily_and_on_change` | Both daily and on data change **(default)** |

The cache duration is computed by `get_cache_duration_hours()` and controls the `valid_until` timestamp on cached `AIInsight` records.

### Best Practices for Tone Tuning

1. **Start conservative** — Fewer sentences, gentle tone. Users prefer concise over verbose.
2. **Test with multiple personas** — Tone guidance interacts with persona instructions. A directive tone_guidance + Gentle Guide persona can create conflicting signals.
3. **Use things_to_avoid liberally** — It is easier to tell the AI what NOT to do than to perfectly describe what to do.
4. **Monitor `AIUsageLog`** — Check token usage after changes. Higher max_tokens = higher API cost.
5. **Check `was_helpful` feedback** — The `AIInsight.was_helpful` field tracks user thumbs-up/down. Low ratings may indicate tone mismatch.

> **Admin Tip:** When adding a new prompt configuration, set it to `is_active = False` first. Preview the composed prompt by calling `config.get_full_prompt()` in the Django shell. Then activate it.

---

## Technical Reference

### Model: `AIPromptConfig`

**Location:** `apps/ai/models.py`
**Table:** `ai_aipromptconfig`

```python
class AIPromptConfig(models.Model):
    prompt_type = models.CharField(max_length=30, unique=True)
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    description = models.TextField(blank=True)
    system_instructions = models.TextField()
    min_sentences = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=2)
    max_sentences = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=4)
    max_tokens = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=150)
    tone_guidance = models.TextField(blank=True)
    things_to_avoid = models.TextField(blank=True)
    example_responses = models.TextField(blank=True)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    refresh_frequency = models.CharField(max_length=30, default='daily_and_on_change')
```

### Prompt Composition

The `get_full_prompt()` method assembles the final prompt:

```python
def get_full_prompt(self) -> str:
    parts = [self.system_instructions]
    parts.append(f"Response length: {self.min_sentences}-{self.max_sentences} sentences.")
    if self.tone_guidance:
        parts.append(f"Tone guidance: {self.tone_guidance}")
    if self.things_to_avoid:
        parts.append(f"IMPORTANT - Avoid: {self.things_to_avoid}")
    return "\n".join(parts)
```

### Cache Invalidation

When an `AIPromptConfig` record is saved, the following caches are cleared:

- `ai_prompt_config_{prompt_type}` — individual config
- `ai_prompt_configs_all` — all configs
- All `system_prompt_*` keys — composed system prompts

This ensures changes take effect within seconds, not hours.

### Fixture

**Location:** `apps/ai/fixtures/ai_prompt_configs.json`

Loaded on deploy. Contains default configurations for all prompt types.

### Interaction with Coaching Styles

The final system prompt sent to OpenAI is composed from multiple layers:

```
Base System Prompt (identity, rules)
  + Coaching Style prompt_instructions (personality)
  + Prompt Config tone_guidance (context-specific tone)
  + Prompt Config things_to_avoid (prohibitions)
  + Dynamic context (user data, current state)
```

All layers are additive. The coaching style sets the personality foundation; the prompt config adds context-specific refinements.

### Values Guardrails

Separate from tone configuration, the **Values Guardrail** system (`ValuesGuardrailPattern` model) provides content filtering. Guardrails are regex-based patterns that detect inappropriate content in both user messages and AI responses. They operate independently of coaching style and tone configuration.

| Severity | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `refuse` | Block the message entirely |
| `redirect` | Gently redirect to appropriate WLJ features |

Guardrails are managed in **Django Admin > AI > Values Guardrail Patterns**.
